data.title: SA Asks: How could Trump's new executive order impact vaccine makers?
data.description:
Earlier this month, President Donald Trump announced an executive order aimed at changing the number and timing of vaccines recommended for children. 

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Stephen Ayers, ALLKA Research, and Gen Alpha how the president's latest executive order could impact vaccine makers. 

Stephen Ayers: Trump's executive order is directionally negative for pediatric vaccine-heavy names, but, in my opinion, it's likely to be challenged and go unimplemented. 

Merck (MRK) arguably has the most exposure with its MMR/MMRV franchise. Splitting the MMR into monovalent shots would completely disrupt its M-M-R II combination jab. Together, ProQuad, M-M-R II, and Varivax generated $592M for Merck in Q2 2026. 

That said, monovalent measles/mumps/rubella vaccines aren't even commercially available in the U.S., and executive orders aren't how vaccine recommendations are legally made. So, if any vaccine names moved on this news, the movement was likely driven by sentiment.

ALLKA Research: On Aug. 10, Trump signed Executive Order 14420, which reduces the number of diseases to 11 for which immunization is recommended for all children. 

By the way, this list does not include the vaccines that protect against hepatitis A/B. I also see no scientific justification for administering the MMR, a combination of mumps, measles, and rubella vaccines, as three separate single-disease shots under the administration's so-called Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations.

Overall, Merck (MRK) and GSK (GSK) are key players in this market. But in addition to MMR vaccines, their portfolios include MMRV vaccines that also protect against varicella (chickenpox). Merck's MMRV vaccine is called ProQuad, while GSK's is marketed as Priorix Tetra. 

Sales of Merck's (MRK) ProQuad/M-M-R II/Varivax were $592M in Q2. Meanwhile, Priorix, Priorix Tetra, and Varilrix generated only $97M in sales for GSK (GSK).

Also, if the policy recommendation by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices is changed to comply with Trump's order, this will certainly be met with resistance, if not litigation, from organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, which could drag on for years.

That's why I can't say with certainty how much Trump's decision will hurt Sanofi (SNY), which is the key manufacturer of hepatitis B vaccines. But in any case, polio/pertussis/Hib primary and booster vaccines, including Heplisav-B, generated less than 6% of the company's revenue in Q2.

Gen Alpha: I expect little to no impact. The executive order isn't law. Vaccine makers will likely continue to manufacture vaccines in their current form. Plus, this isn't likely to change public perception on vaccines, as most parents likely already have their own stance on them.

(Gen Alpha is also a contributor to the SA investing group iREIT®+HOYA Capital.)

data.title: Key deals this week: Stripe, KKR, Virtu and more
data.description:
Stripe (STRIP) announced a deal to buy the AI model gateway and routing platform OpenRouter. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. However, a Bloomberg report had said the acquisition consideration could be over $7B.

Madison Air Solutions (MAIR) to acquire ebm-papst at an enterprise purchase price of $5.4B, or $5.0B net of future tax savings, according to a statement on Monday.

Virtu Financial (VIRT) was considering a sale of its agency brokerage and technology division. The potential transaction could be worth up to $3.5B to $4B, one of the people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News. The divestiture is expected to free up capital to invest in the company's core market-making operation, according to the people who asked not to be identified because the information is private. 

An investor group led by affiliates of KKR (KKR) and Dragoneer Investment Group, plus Amwins Group, agreed to acquire Australian insurance company Steadfast Group (SFGLF) for ~A$7.7B (US$5.5B), the company said in a filing on Friday.

Bunker Hill Mining (BHLL) to acquire Silver47 Exploration in an all-stock deal valued at ~$163M, forming a larger U.S. silver and critical minerals producer. The merger will combine Bunker Hill's (BHLL) working mine in the Silver Valley of Idaho with Silver47's silver-focused U.S. exploration and development pipeline in Alaska, Nevada, and New Mexico.

Mitsubishi Electric (MIELY) to acquire PCI Energy Solutions, a U.S.-based provider of enterprise software for energy management and optimization, for $1.4B. Mitsubishi will acquire 100% of PCI’s equity interests under the agreement signed on Aug. 20, 2026.

Veralto (VLTO) to acquire Cleanwater1 for $465M, or ~$452M net of estimated tax benefits, with closing expected in Q4 2026. Cleanwater1 provides on-site hypochlorite disinfection, solids management and odor filtration technologies, with roughly 25,000 units installed across water and industrial applications.

data.title: Canada retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods to take effect on Sept. 8
data.description:
Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Saturday that his country will impose retaliatory tariffs on a wide range of U.S. imports starting from September 8 in response to the Trump administration’s new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods.

A raft of American-made goods, including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and ​paper, and electronics, will be affected by the retaliatory tariffs, Carney said, adding that duties will also impact products ​currently ⁠subject to the unjustified Section 232 and 338 tariffs. Details of specific products subject to new tariffs are expected to be available in the coming days.

His remarks came after weeks of trade negotiations between the two sides collapsed late Friday night and the new U.S. tariffs that could impact roughly $20B worth of Canadian exports took effect immediately.

Minutes before the deadline, Carney said that Canada will impose "dollar for dollar" reciprocal tariffs on American goods, noting that “last-minute changes in the U.S. proposed terms were unfair and uneconomic and called into question the reliability of any deal.”

During a press conference from the Parliament building in Ottawa, Carney detailed reasons that prompted Canada to withdraw from the talks. "We ⁠cannot ​accept what they have offered, and ​we will not give what they have asked," he added.

According to Carney, the U.S. proposals included a plan to limit tariffs “to autos only [and] ... not include medium and heavy-duty trucks, which is a big change.” Another reason was last-minute efforts sought by the U.S. that would “restrict our ability to have other trade deals."

U.S. trade representatives also tried to “restrict our protections of our language, our culture, and in effect, our sovereignty,” Carney said without providing details on that dispute. “It was also a cumulative aspect, as I mentioned in my remarks, about the willingness in total to enter into a true economic partnership,” he added.

In a press call shortly before midnight on Friday, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that Canada refused to “finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week.” “Despite the U.S. offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walkbacks of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days,” Greer added.

data.title: General Motors inks tentative labor deals with Canada’s Unifor union
data.description:
Canadian labor union Unifor on Saturday announced that it has reached tentative agreements with General Motors (GM) covering more than 4,600 of its members working across four manufacturing facilities of the U.S. automaker.

Unifor members at Oshawa Assembly Plant, St. Catharines Propulsion Plant, Woodstock Parts Distribution Centre, and CAMI Assembly are covered by the new deals, the terms of which were not immediately available.

“Our bargaining committee worked diligently to reach these agreements, which deliver strong income and benefit gains, amid some of the most challenging times in our history,” Unifor National President Lana Payne said.

The agreements, which were unanimously endorsed by the Unifor General Motors Master Bargaining Committee, still require ratification by its members in meetings scheduled for Aug. 29-Aug. 30, the union said.

Unifor, the largest private-sector union in Canada, started contract negotiations with General Motors (GM) last week after finalizing a three-year labor agreement with Ford Motor (F) in July.

Beginning with Ford (F), Unifor started labor talks with the Detroit ​Three automakers in June as it sought to negotiate new contracts ahead of a Sept. 20 expiration of existing collective agreements.

data.description:

  • Micron Technology (MU) EVP and Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana sold 15,000 shares at $934.29 each for $14.01M. The transaction represented about 6.70% of his holdings, leaving him with 209,021 shares.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week as several headlines from companies including Nvidia, Micron and Super Micro Computer (SMCI) grabbed the focus of investors.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the green on Friday in tandem with other indexes on Wall Street.

For the week, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) fell roughly over 3% during the week. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • Jack Henry & Associates (JKHY) +8.41%
  • Gartner (IT) +8.18%
  • Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) +8%
  • Marvell Technology (MRVL) +6.77%
  • Tyler Technologies (TYL) +6.72%

Top Losers:

  • Jabil (JBL) -13.74%
  • Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) -12.68%
  • Flex (FLEX) -12.45%
  • Intel (INTC) -12.13%
  • Akamai (AKAM) -11.66%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Nvidia pledges $100B backing for OpenAI's Ohio data center

Nvidia (NVDA) has agreed to provide more than $100B in credit support to backstop a massive new OpenAI (OPENAI) data center campus in Pike County, Ohio.

The project is being developed, owned, and operated by SB Energy, a SoftBank Group (SFTBY) subsidiary, with OpenAI signing a 20-year lease as the anchor tenant, according to a report by the Financial Times. As part of the transaction, Nvidia will also make a $1.5B direct equity investment in SB Energy.

Under the terms of the deal, Nvidia will serve as the exclusive supplier of AI computing systems for the site, potentially generating $150B to $200B in hardware revenue as the facility expands to house over 1M Nvidia chips, the report noted.

Broadcom engages with lenders to secure $60B for AI chip financing

Broadcom (AVGO) is reportedly engaged in discussions with Blackstone and Apollo Global Management (APO) to raise more than $60B in debt in a deal that will benefit the Claude-maker Anthropic (ANTHRO). According to Bloomberg, the deal might include a $30B junior debt tranche and a senior-secured tranche and Broadcom would likely secure a portion of the senior-secured tranche.

Micron shows off U.S.-based Micron Research Labs

Micron Technology (MU) showed off its new U.S.-based Micron Research Labs, which is backed by a $10B investment and will be a new research hub for memory and AI.

The $10B investment in the hub will be made over the next decade and will bring customers, academics, government and the semiconductor industry to look for breakthroughs. Key areas of research include memory technologies, advanced memory and compute, packaging, and chip manufacturing. It will live on Micron's campus in Boise, Idaho, Micron added.

Other notable headlines include Nebius Group (NBIS) announcing its intention to offer $4.50 billion aggregate original principal amount of $4.50 billion of convertible senior notes.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) was in the spotlight after the AI server maker completed its independent investigation into the alleged smuggling scheme and said its senior management was unaware of the actions. In May, Super Micro said it was working with Taiwanese authorities to prevent illegal smuggling of its server technology.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Apple, Merck and Analog Devices among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, as Treasury yields held mostly steady and Bitcoin (BTC-USD) saw sharp swings.

Nasdaq (COMP:IND) fell 2% for the week, while the Dow (DJI) declined 1.3%.

Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Analog Devices upgraded to Outperform after Q3 results

Analog Devices' (ADI) was upgraded to Outperform from Market Perform by Bernstein after the company’s third-quarter results featured solid revenue growth across all of its segments, including Industrial, Automotive, Communications and Consumer.

"Upside in the quarter was broad-based but came from Automotive in particular, with Industrial, Consumer and Comms also above expectations," said Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon and increased price target to $465 from $430.

Bernstein increased its full fiscal year 2026 EPS estimate to $12.85 from $12.40 and fiscal 2027 to $16.77 from $14.65.

Apple upgraded at Rothschild on product strength

Apple (AAPL) was upgraded at Rothschild to Buy from Hold, with the investment firm citing its product strength and its potential entry into the foldable handset market.

“Apple Intelligence has been disappointing,” analysts at the firm wrote in a note to clients.  The analysts put a $400 price target on Apple.

“We examine January's belated adoption of the well-established 'Fast Follower' playbook, which will be improved by an Apple Intelligence refresh in September. We evaluate the benefits a bolder Fast Follower 2.0 strategy might bring, concluding CEO-elect John Ternus would benefit from considering a closer cooperation with Nvidia (Buy),” the firm said.

Merck upgraded at Morgan Stanley; RBC downgrades

Morgan Stanley upgraded Merck (MRK) to Overweight from Equal Weight, indicating that the company is now better equipped to face a 2028 patent cliff for its blockbuster therapy, Keytruda, given the trial success for the personalized melanoma vaccine known as intismeran autogene.

“Our new base case implies flattish revenues (vs. -5% prior) following the Keytruda LOE in 2028, while our bull case implies a ~4% 2030–2035 CAGR, meaning MRK could grow from its 2029 trough if current pipeline programs are successful,” analyst Terence Flynn wrote and raised its price target on MRK to $89 from $39.

However, RBC Capital Markets downgraded the stock, citing valuation concerns. The firm raised price target on Merck to $150 from $142 per share.

Wells Fargo upgrades Okta on signs of improving demand, execution

Wells Fargo upgraded Okta (OKTA) to Overweight from Equal-Weight and increased its price target to $180 from $150, citing signs of improving demand and execution in its core business.

“Increasing body of evidence in support of core demand improving; view low-teens growth as likely base case, rather than upside. Identity's rise in investment priority has become a clear recurring theme in our survey & field work—most recently, partners ranked Identity as the #2 spend priority (behind only AI; up from #4 last quarter),” Wells Fargo analyst Richard Poland wrote.

Workday (WDAY) was downgraded by Deutsche Bank to Hold from Buy as the investment firm said the risk-reward is “more balanced” after shares rose recently following reports of a potential acquisition by private equity.

Morgan Stanley downgraded Baidu (BIDU) to Underweight from Equal-weight, citing weak advertising revenue and rising investment in artificial intelligence. The brokerage cut its price target to $80 from $130.

GF Securities upped its price target on Nvidia (NVDA) ahead of its upcoming earnings report, and Wedbush Securities weighed in on the OpenAI (OPENAI) guarantee. GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu raised his price target on Nvidia to $345 from $308 and reiterated his Buy rating, as he is expecting a “strong” Vera Rubin sales cycle.

data.title: TikTok to pay $400M to settle DOJ's child privacy case
data.description:
TikTok (TIKTOK) and its Chinese parent, ByteDance (BDNCE), have reached a $400M settlement with the U.S. Department of Justice to resolve a 2024 lawsuit alleging that the social media platform violated federal laws related to children's privacy.

The DOJ said Friday that TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and another $100 million after an order vacates an earlier consent decree against its predecessor company, Musical.ly.

“This settlement is a major victory for American children and parents,” said U.S. Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. in a statement. “The Department’s priority is ensuring that children are protected online and that companies entrusted with their personal information meet their legal obligations. This resolution secures a substantial recovery while reinforcing the protections that families expect and deserve.”

Since the DOJ's lawsuit in 2024, TikTok has undergone major changes, most notably in the ownership structure of its U.S. arm. In January, the social video platform company signed agreements with major investors including Oracle (ORCL), Silver Lake, and the Emirati investment firm MGX to form the new TikTok U.S. joint venture.

Representatives for TikTok did not immediately respond to a message for comment Friday.

The latest lawsuit focused on allegations that TikTok and its China-based parent company, ByteDance, violated a federal law that requires kid-oriented apps and websites to get parental consent before collecting personal information of children under 13. It also says the companies failed to honor requests from parents who wanted their children’s accounts deleted and chose not to delete accounts even when the firms knew they belonged to kids under 13.

The settlement comes as social media companies face an avalanche of lawsuits over children's safety and privacy and a growing number of countries are banning young kids and teens from social media apps. Instagram's parent company, Meta Platforms (META), is currently on trial in federal court in Oakland, California, over allegations it violated the 1998 Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act, or COPPA, along with various state statutes.

The Associated Press contributed to this story.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: All 12 key S&P 500 reporting firms top EPS estimates; 11 deliver Y/Y growth
data.description:
Corporate earnings this week featured a high-stakes lineup of reports from 12 notable companies across the consumer discretionary, consumer staples, information technology, industrials, and financials sectors.

Earnings Roundup:

  • Bottom Line: All 12 reporting companies beat consensus earnings estimates, with 11 delivering year-over-year profit expansion.

  • Top Line: Revenue performance remained strong, as 11 companies topped Wall Street expectations and all 12 achieved year-over-year top-line growth (leaving 1 firm missing consensus estimates).

 

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

  • The Home Depot (HD) traded flat post-earnings despite delivering reported strong second-quarter results double beat, with revenue of $47.9 billion, a 5.8% increase from last year, and adjusted earnings per share of $4.92. Comparable sales rose 1.7%, and average ticket size increased to $92.50. For fiscal year 2026, projected sales growth is 2.5% to 4.5%, comp sales growth of 0% to 2%, and EPS growth of 0% to 4%, with expected IEEPA tariff refunds helping to offset elevated input and fuel costs.
  • Lowe's (LOW) rose 2.02% post-earnings after trimming its full-year revenue outlook, even as second-quarter results beat expectations. Adjusted EPS rose to $4.40 (beating $4.22 consensus) on sales driven by Pro, online (+15.7%), and home services growth. However, softer DIY spending limited comparable sales growth to 0.2% and narrowed the gross margin by 80 bps to 33.0%. Citing dynamic macro conditions, Lowe's lowered its full-year sales forecast to ~$92.0B (vs. $92.9B consensus) and set adjusted EPS guidance at $12.25 (vs. $12.43 consensus).
  • Walmart (WMT) shares dropped 9.15% after not meeting U.S. same-store sales growth expectations, despite reporting strong Q2 earnings. U.S. sales grew by 2.6%, lower than the 3.7% expected, while Sam's Club and international sales performed well. However, shares faced pressure as soft guidance fell short of Wall Street forecasts, with Q3 EPS projected at $0.62–$0.64 (vs. $0.69 consensus) and full-year EPS guided to $2.80–$2.87 (vs. $2.90 consensus).
  • Target (TGT) rose 4.28% post-earnings after delivering a strong second-quarter double beat, with revenue rising 5.3% to $26.54 billion and non-GAAP EPS at $4.11. This was supported by a 3.8% increase in comparable sales and 3.6% more foot traffic. Target raised its full-year sales growth forecast to ~5% and adjusted EPS estimate to $9.90–$10.90 (vs. $8.47 consensus). Operating income margin is projected at ~6.0% for the full year.
  • Analog Devices (ADI) shares dropped 1% post-earnings despite delivering a fiscal Q3 double beat led by strong Data Center and Industrial demand, with revenue surging 39.6% year-over-year to $4.02B (beating by $90M) and non-GAAP EPS reaching $3.45 (topping estimates by $0.11). Buoyed by this momentum, the company issued upbeat fiscal Q4 guidance, projecting revenue of $4.3B (±$100M) vs. $4.08B consensus and adjusted EPS of $3.86 (±$0.15) vs. $3.55 consensus, alongside an expected adjusted operating margin of ~52.0%.
  • The TJX Companies (TJX) dipped 4.21% post-earnings despite delivering a Q2 double beat, with revenue up 5.4% to $15.2 billion and EPS at $1.22, exceeding expectations. Comparable sales grew 4%, led by HomeGoods and international markets. TJX raised its full-year EPS guidance to $5.31–$5.36 (vs. $5.23 consensus) on expected comp sales growth of 2% to 3%, while announcing plans to accelerate annual store openings to 4% starting next year.

Earnings Next Week

As earnings season rolls on, market attention turns to pivotal results across enterprise software, cybersecurity, retail, and semiconductors to assess AI monetization trends and consumer resilience.

Upcoming highlights include mega-cap technology and AI leader Nvidia (NVDA), software giants Salesforce (CRM), Workday (WDAY), Intuit (INTU), and Autodesk (ADSK), cybersecurity pure-play CrowdStrike (CRWD), and semiconductor leader Marvell Technology (MRVL), alongside design automation firm Synopsys (SNPS) and life sciences player Agilent Technologies (A).

Retail and consumer demand will also take center stage with updates from major discount and specialty retailers, including Dollar General (DG), Dollar Tree (DLTR), Best Buy (BBY), Ulta Beauty (ULTA), and Williams-Sonoma (WSM), along with tech hardware maker HP Inc. (HPQ), healthcare tech supplier Veeva Systems (VEEV), and packaged food staples The J. M. Smucker Company (SJM) and Hormel Foods (HRL).

data.title: Paramount to meet California AG in a bid to settle case over Warner deal: Variety
data.description:
Representatives from Paramount (PSKY) are scheduled to meet with the California Attorney General’s office on Monday as part of an effort to settle the states' antitrust case over its $111B merger deal with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), Variety reported.

The blockbuster M&A deal, which would unite two of Hollywood’s five legacy studios and two of the three leading U.S. cable programmers, is currently on hold pending the outcome of a trial in a federal court in California.

Earlier this month, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín, based in Oakland, set a March trial date after a lawsuit challenging the deal was filed by 12 state attorneys general led by California AG Rob Bonta.

AG Bonta has indicated his support for a settlement but accused Paramount (PSKY) of failing to agree with the kind of structural solutions that would satisfy the states’ demands.

The news of potential settlement talks comes after Judge Martinez-Olguin asked the parties to name two potential magistrate judges who could preside over the mediation by next Wednesday. Paramount (SPKY) and the California AG’s press office didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
